chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, and from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was killed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) commanded Fatimah (peace be upon her) to prepare food for Asma bint Umays for three days, and to go to her with her womenfolk, and stay with her for three days. Thus, the Sunnah became established that food be prepared for the bereaved for three days.

key_terms.أَسْمَاءَ بِنْتِ عُمَيْسٍ: Asma bint Umays, a companion of the Prophet and wife of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْمُصِيبَةِ: The people of the calamity/mourning, referring to the bereaved family
key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: The Sunnah, the established practice or tradition of the Prophet
key_terms.جَعْفَرُ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, a prominent companion of the Prophet known as Ja'far al-Tayyar
key_terms.طَعَامٌ: Food, specifically prepared meals for the mourners

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic tradition regarding providing food for the bereaved family after a death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s directive to Fatimah al-Zahra to provide sustenance for Asma bint Umays, establishing the enduring Sunnah of preparing food for the bereaved family for three days. In Shia scholarly tradition, this act is viewed not merely as charity but as a practical manifestation of communal support (ta'ziyah) during the initial period of grief, relieving the family from the burden of cooking while they mourn. The narration underscores the Prophet's emphasis on tangible care for the household of the deceased, reinforcing the social obligations of neighbors and kin in times of loss.
